pr_body:
Fixes #90071

When we enable `Activity.Baggage` logging, we currently log it as a scope object that implements `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string?>>`. The problem is that many logger providers don't support scopes of this type, causing them to use the `ToString()` method instead of properly enumerating the items and logging them correctly. To address this issue, we are making a fix by changing the baggage scope object to implement `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object?>>`. This change will ensure compatibility with most logger providers, allowing them to enumerate the baggage items and log each entry separately as intended.

issue_context.title: Activity Tracking option for logger factory works differently for tags and baggage
comments: This issue has been marked `needs-author-action` and may be missing some important information.

> @yoziv what kind of logger and `IExternalScopeProvider` is used to produce the output you are showing?

It can be reproduced with the [Console Exporter for OpenTelemetry](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/main/src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Console/README.md) and [Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerFactoryScopeProvider](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Logging/src/LoggerFactoryScopeProvider.cs).

The problem is in OpenTelemetry code https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/a831093ae18efeb7bcbcef1042d05c0cef05e7a8/src/OpenTelemetry/Logs/LogRecordScope.cs#L63. It doesn't handle the case `IEnumrable<KeyValuePair<string, string>>` and at that time will just use [`ToString`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/blob/a831093ae18efeb7bcbcef1042d05c0cef05e7a8/src/OpenTelemetry/Logs/LogRecordScope.cs#L71) to log the scope which produce the logger output you are seeing there. Note the Baggage scope object is defined as `private sealed class ActivityBaggageLogScopeWrapper : IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string?>>`

@CodeBlanch you may confirm and move this issue to OpenTelemetry repo.
@cakescience yes, we can fix that. are you interested to submit a PR to fix that?
I don't think I'll have the time, but thanks for the proposal!

I chatted with @tarekgh offline about this. My feedback was (more or less)...

IMO the best fix is to update [this custom TState](https://source.dot.net/#Microsoft.Extensions.Logging/LoggerFactoryScopeProvider.cs,223) to implement `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object>>` (`IReadOnlyList` would be even better for perf in OTel).

Because support for `KeyValuePair<string, object>` seems to be ubiquitous. `OpenTelemetry` and `runtime` support that convention, as does [Serilog](https://github.com/serilog/serilog-extensions-logging/blob/b524ab61765c7576971563355b5e68d8cd769ed9/src/Serilog.Extensions.Logging/Extensions/Logging/SerilogLoggerScope.cs#L80-L107). I didn't check other `ILoggerProvider` implementations, but I suspect we will find the same.

I did a quick search through aspnetcore and it was turning up consistent as well for custom scope TStates:

* https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/55fa3024d23666e3301ddc06f349febac8f98449/src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/src/MvcCoreLoggerExtensions.cs#L280
* https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/55fa3024d23666e3301ddc06f349febac8f98449/src/HealthChecks/HealthChecks/src/HealthCheckLogScope.cs#L10
* https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/55fa3024d23666e3301ddc06f349febac8f98449/src/Mvc/Mvc.ViewFeatures/src/ViewComponents/DefaultViewComponentInvoker.cs#L284

A couple other notes:

* The [docs show using KeyValuePair<string, object>](https://github.com/dotnet/docs/blob/444753733df757d910cb9a7d46ea11eadcdd245b/docs/core/extensions/logging.md?plain=1#L478).
* The [proposed fix in OpenTelemetry is expensive](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-dotnet/pull/4746/files#diff-27f9c77032025b8e7903e44874f67a07845bf202bfe6f9a47bfdfb7baa1cf5e3R69) costing a list allocation and an enumerator allocation and CPU to copy things.

review_comments: Isn't this a breaking change to remove an interface implementation that was previously available? Should we implement both IEnumerable interfaces?

I don't think this is breaking. the worst case that if there is a provider which handle `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string?>>` and not handling `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object?>>`. This is very unlikely because they will not be handling most supported cases anyway and we are not seeing this in most providers we are aware of.

Do we make any specific guarantees in the BCL that exposed types won't change their interfaces? I agree with you that I don't expect popular logging providers to break. Even if this is technically a breaking change its probably not an impactful one. I think its more a question do we need to document this as a breaking change in behavior?

> Do we make any specific guarantees in the BCL that exposed types won't change their interfaces? 

This is exposed as object but not as public API. Nothing in the scope object itself even gives any indication this is produced by Activity.Baggage either. 

> I think its more a question do we need to document this as a breaking change in behavior?

We can document it, but I am seeing this as a extremely low priority for now. We still have the option to document it in the future as breaking charge if we see any complaint. I am fine if you think otherwise and should file breaking change anyway.
If we don't have any previous rules around it I'm happy to wait and only do it in response to a complaint. Thanks!
